_readme: The web of projects on /stack and the 'How it fits' box on each product page. Nodes are the dots; x/y place them in the 960x560 diagram. Links are proven integrations only: each one must point at something real in the repos. status 'planned' draws dashed and says so. 'story' is a case study URL, when one exists. Chapters are the build order, oldest first. Dates come from git history.

links.says: Drafts the posts for every Pheidi merge, for @pheiditraining on X, Bluesky, and Mastodon.
First real customer. A Pheidi PR where three cards disagreed about one channel rebuilt Merge & Tell's PR page.
Hosts Pheidi's docs screenshots, Play Store shots, and listing video. A test fails the build if the pictures and the pages drift apart.
The worked example in Screenery's own CI-setup tests.
sync-docs, the skill that keeps docs honest, was born in Pheidi and ported into NightForge.
Runs Pheidi's weekly docs sweep, nightly error sweep, and CodeRabbit re-reviews.
Runs Merge & Tell's weekly docs sweep and CodeRabbit re-reviews.
Runs the Auspex Fatalis docs sweep through its own sync-docs port.
Reshoots every Merge & Tell screen on each merge. Public pages use Screenery shots by name, as a rule.
Posts a screenshot gallery on every Auspex Fatalis pull request, and serves the help-article images.
Every live screenshot on this site. Nobody here exports a PNG by hand.
Writes the 'Recent updates' on the product pages here, from the PRs that shipped them.
Drafts the posts for Auspex Fatalis merges, steered by the repo's .marketing.yml.

Screenery's merges get drafted posts too.
NightForge's skill changes get drafted posts too.

chapters.title: I needed a running plan
chapters.body: Pheidi started in 2019 as an Angular toy, then sat untouched for five years. In March 2026 I restarted it with a spec and a team of agents. It's past 700 commits since then. Plans that bend when you get hurt or go on vacation, which is exactly what I needed.

chapters.title: Then nobody heard about it
chapters.body: Pheidi was shipping every day and telling zero people. I'd merge a two-day fix and already be on the next branch. So I built Merge & Tell: every merged PR becomes a drafted post, and I only have to say yes.

chapters.title: Then the robots drifted
chapters.body: Now I had several repos, each with a hand-written nightly sweep that read the error logs and opened fixes. In about two months they drifted into three different pipelines. One rediscovered its whole backlog every night. NightForge is the one pipeline they all run now.

chapters.title: Then the screenshots went stale
chapters.body: Docs, store listings, product pages, and Merge & Tell posts all wanted pictures of the app. Mine were frozen PNGs from whenever someone last remembered. Screenery makes CI push them and gives each one a URL that updates on release. Spec to published CLI in under two weeks.

chapters.title: And then this site
chapters.body: The page you're reading pulls its screenshots from Screenery and its update notes from Merge & Tell. It's less a portfolio and more the place where all of it lands.
